newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-MANCINI'S LATE GOAL BITTER BLOW TO HODGSON'S INTER.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MANCINI'S LATE GOAL BITTER BLOW TO HODGSON'S INTER.

text.p: When Inter president Massimo Moratti tried and failed to buy Roberto Mancini earlier this season, coach Roy Hodgson uttered the famous words: "Mancini who?".

On Sunday, the most prolific striker currently playing serie A soccer delivered Hodgson a painful reminder of his credentials, scoring Sampdoria's winner two minutes from time in a dramatic 4-3 victory at the San Siro.
Mancini's goal -- his 132nd league goal -- completed a dramatic comeback for Sampdoria who had trailed 3-1. Worse for Hodgson, it also dealt a severe blow to Inter's title challenge.
The Milan side now lie fifth in the table, seven points behind league leaders Juventus, who came from two goals down to defeat Verona 3-2.
Juventus now have 28 points from 13 matches, six clear of their nearest challengers Vicenza, in action later tonight.
In a thrilling match, Sampdoria made the perfect start, edging in front with a goal from Vincenzo Montella in the seventh minute.

Inter drew level through Marco Branca in the 13th, took the lead with a close range shot from Nicola Berti in the 43rd and looked to have sealed victory with Branca's second goal straight after the break.
At this stage, Mancini, whose move to Inter was vetoed by his club, took over.

In the 56th minute, he set up Montella's second with a pinpoint cross, then, after Marco Franceschetti had levelled the scores in the 85th minute, Sampdoria's captain delivered the coup de grace from close-range.
"I don't know if the goal means anything more or less to him but it was like a film," said Sampdoria coach Sven Goran Eriksson.
After the match, angry fans hurled stones that shattered windows in the VIP lounge at the San Siro. "I understand their anger," said Hogdson, "it was a very, very bad result for us."
Hodgson's mood hardly improved as news filtered through of Juve's comeback at the Stadio delle Alpi.
The European champions were given a shock when Felippo Maniero finished off swift Verona counter-attacks in clinical fashion in the 25th and 44th minutes.
Without injured striker Alen Boksic, it was left to defender Sergio Porrini to pull Juve back into the game with an untidy goal on the brink of half-time.

After the break, Alessandro Del Piero levelled the scores when he calmly slotted home a penalty; then, in the 72nd minute, the same player unleashed a vicious, curling shot from 20 metres to brilliantly clinch Juve's fourth successive league win.
"The difference between us and Juventus today lay in the class of Del Piero," said Verona manager Luigi Cagni.
AC Milan climbed to third on 21 points after their second successive league victory under Arrigo Sacchi -- courtesy of three goals from Italy's Demetrio Albertini at bottom-of-the-table Reggiana.
But Sacchi was wary of title talk. "This victory is down to the players and my predecessor (Oscar Washington Tabarez)," said Sacchi. "No manager can turn a team round in ten days."
Milan lie level on 21 points with Inter and Bologna, held 2-2 at Cagliari.
